concepts.name: Native versus cross-platform apps
concepts.summary: Explain how native, cross-platform and web-based apps differ and what trade-offs each brings for a simple app.

concepts.name: App project structure
concepts.summary: Identify the main parts of a mobile project: source code, resources, manifest or configuration, and build files.

concepts.name: Screens and UI components
concepts.summary: Describe how a screen is composed from components such as text, buttons, images and input fields.

concepts.name: Touch input and events
concepts.summary: Understand how taps and gestures on components trigger event handlers in code.

concepts.name: Platform ecosystems and SDKs
concepts.summary: Name the main platforms, their languages and IDEs, and the role of the SDK.

concepts.name: Emulators and device testing
concepts.summary: Recall how to run and view an app on an emulator, simulator or physical phone.

concepts.name: App lifecycle states
concepts.summary: Explain that an app moves between running, background and terminated states and why this matters on phones.

misconceptions.text: A mobile app runs continuously like a desktop program once it has been opened.
An app written for Android will run unchanged on iOS.
Testing in an emulator is enough to know the app works on real phones.

concepts.name: Layout containers and constraints
concepts.summary: Arrange components with rows, columns and constraints so a screen looks right at different sizes.

concepts.name: Screen navigation stack
concepts.summary: Move between screens, pass data to them and handle the back action using a navigation stack.

concepts.name: Component state and re-rendering
concepts.summary: Hold changing values in state and update the screen when that state changes.

concepts.name: Lists and adapters
concepts.summary: Display scrollable collections efficiently by binding data items to reusable row views.

concepts.name: Lifecycle callbacks
concepts.summary: Place setup and cleanup code in the correct lifecycle callbacks of a screen or app.

concepts.name: Simple local persistence
concepts.summary: Save and reload small settings or values using the platform's key-value storage.

concepts.name: Fetching remote data
concepts.summary: Call a REST endpoint asynchronously, parse the JSON and show the result on screen.

misconceptions.text: Changing a variable that holds screen data automatically updates what the user sees.
Network calls can be made on the main UI thread without noticeable effect.
Data kept in memory survives the app being closed or the screen being rotated.

concepts.name: Architecture patterns for apps
concepts.summary: Separate UI, presentation logic and data access, and analyse how a pattern such as MVVM organises responsibilities.

concepts.name: Runtime permissions
concepts.summary: Request and handle permissions for camera, location or notifications, including denial and rationale flows.

concepts.name: Device sensors and hardware APIs
concepts.summary: Use device features such as location or camera through platform APIs while managing battery and privacy cost.

concepts.name: Structured local databases
concepts.summary: Model, store and query structured data locally with a database layer and schema migrations.

concepts.name: Concurrency and async work
concepts.summary: Run network and disk work off the main thread and diagnose problems such as race conditions and UI freezes.

concepts.name: Repository and offline caching
concepts.summary: Combine remote and local sources behind a repository so the app works with poor or no connectivity.

concepts.name: Handling errors and loading states
concepts.summary: Represent loading, success, empty and failure states and show appropriate feedback to the user.

concepts.name: Push and local notifications
concepts.summary: Implement notifications and understand how a push message reaches a device through the platform service.

misconceptions.text: Putting all logic in the screen class is fine because the app is small.
If the user denies a permission, the app can ask again as often as it likes and the feature still must work.
Offline support just means catching the network error and showing a message.

concepts.name: Authentication and secure storage
concepts.summary: Evaluate sign-in flows and choose secure storage for tokens and sensitive data on the device.

concepts.name: Adaptive and accessible design
concepts.summary: Judge how well a design supports tablets, screen readers, dynamic text size and multiple languages.

concepts.name: Crash reporting and analytics
concepts.summary: Instrument an app to analyse crashes and user behaviour while respecting privacy.

concepts.name: Performance profiling and optimisation
concepts.summary: Use profilers to find slow rendering, memory leaks and excess work, and fix their causes.

concepts.name: Dependency injection and modularity
concepts.summary: Assess how injecting dependencies and splitting modules improves testability and build times.

concepts.name: Automated testing strategy
concepts.summary: Decide what to cover with unit, integration and UI tests and judge the cost and reliability of each.

concepts.name: Build variants and CI/CD
concepts.summary: Configure environments, signing and automated builds so releases are repeatable.

concepts.name: Store release and review compliance
concepts.summary: Prepare listings, privacy declarations and staged rollouts, and analyse common causes of review rejection.

misconceptions.text: Storing tokens in ordinary preferences is safe because other apps cannot read app storage.
Performance tuning should be done up front on every screen rather than guided by profiling.
Accessibility and localisation can be added at the end without redesign.

concepts.name: Cross-platform strategy design
concepts.summary: Evaluate native, shared-logic and fully cross-platform approaches against product, team and performance constraints.

concepts.name: Scalable app architecture design
concepts.summary: Design an app architecture that lets many teams ship features independently with clear boundaries.

concepts.name: Offline sync and conflict resolution
concepts.summary: Create a synchronisation design that handles conflicts, retries and partial failure between device and server.

concepts.name: Release engineering and feature flags
concepts.summary: Create a release process using flags, staged rollouts and rollback to reduce risk of shipping.

concepts.name: Mobile security threat modelling
concepts.summary: Assess threats such as tampering, insecure transport and data leakage, and judge which defences are worth their cost.

concepts.name: Platform evolution and migration
concepts.summary: Judge when and how to adopt new OS APIs and migrate legacy code without breaking users.

concepts.name: Energy and resource budgeting
concepts.summary: Evaluate background work, networking and sensor use against battery, data and OS restrictions across a device range.

misconceptions.text: A cross-platform framework always lowers cost compared with native development.
Last-write-wins is an adequate sync strategy for any data.
Obfuscation and certificate pinning make an app's secrets safe on the device.
